remaining_concerns: No genuinely new admissible evidence was provided; the Actor narrowed and caveated the same summarized record.
The audit still lacks the underlying text for BPROC-011-B through BPROC-011-E, so the key predicate of materiality cannot be independently verified from admissible evidence available to this role.

Under the stated policy, quality-process gaps and questionnaire/storage inconsistencies support follow-up or escalation, but do not by themselves establish reject-level grounds; the current summary does not clearly show why the combined record crossed that threshold.
The procurement analyst's recommendation is described as conditional follow-up before approval, which is closer to a hold/escalation signal than clear proof that rejection was policy-sufficient.
The prior performance point remains modest support only and does not materially strengthen the rejection theory.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and instead offered a narrower interpretation of the same summarized record. That reinterpretation is more disciplined than an overbroad claim of confirmed control failure, and it appropriately concedes the evidentiary limits. But proportional narrowing is not enough here to reach compliant_with_caveats, because the unresolved compliance predicate is not merely overstatement; it is whether the admissible record available to this role actually shows a material unresolved risk sufficient to support rejection rather than follow-up or escalation. On the available summaries alone, that remains unverified and uncertain. The Actor's caveated framing reduces overclaiming, but it does not cure the absence of independently assessable evidence establishing reject-level materiality under the policy.
